revised.summary:
The Patterns and PlayMap halves of the Stagewatch interop, ranked by show risk and cut into units each repo's process can take, revised after the critique. The full design is in /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/patterns-playmap-side.md. §10 answers each critique item: all 17 issues and the missing reader were accepted. Four were adjusted:
- Patterns' messages have no urgency.
- The rig option is peers-not-screens' --node-keys.
- backups/ is not in the support bundle.
- An unknown key-shaped key gets 401 from /api/context.
I also closed one hole the critic did not name: a key that was never bound never goes to a target chosen by a wire line.

TIER A, now
(1) G04, Patterns Round 89.1.
- The stuck beat sets a flag that only the receive loop writes. The context moves to its own field, written only by the beat task, so a context fetch can no longer restore the live frame.
- The Sight getter folds the flag in: Frame.Live=false.
- Every reader then shows no time and a red light: pages, STATE, the twin relay, the Eye, the Nodes card, the brief, the module and the log (one line per transition).
- If Stagewatch is stuck before its first frame, the desk's own timer keeps running.
(2) G09, Patterns Round 89.2-89.3.
- A private address becomes kept://host:port/<id>. The id is 60 random bits from a CSPRNG, kept in a per-machine book, so a 4-digit ?pin= can no longer be brute-forced from what is published.
- The real URL stays in SettingsStore.BaseDirectory.
- The twin carries the book under TwinConfig.SendSecrets, so a standby that takes over still draws the page.
- Readers covered: the OSC status line, the navigate-failure log, the native player, and the support bundle (redacted).
- The fence test now includes a takeover leg. The WebView2 probe (L26) lands too.
(3)-(4) G47, G12's air half and G25 on PlayMap.
- These are now an explicit request for the owner's exception (PM-X). It quotes round 3 §4 in full: a file no wave names may not be edited. They are not presented as allowed by the rule.
- If declined, they wait for the integration pass.
- G47 also cleans existing pass-bearing items at engine start.
- G25 fits by bytes only. Over 64 KiB it trims in order: recent texts to 200 characters (Stagewatch's reader keeps no more), then command words, then green items. A context under 64 KiB is posted unchanged.
- Stagewatch answers 413 after reading the body (bounded), and the upload and script paths are exempt.

TIER B
- G21: while following, the speaker message goes through Stagewatch only when the link holds a node key. Otherwise it goes to this desk's displays and says so, so a cue step never fails.
  - Flash maps to slow or off.
  - The receipt's stage is read: an 'accepted' receipt is not reported as on screen.
  - CLEAR clears only messages Patterns itself sent.
  - Messages go on their own lane, latest wins.
  - The page draws one message, latest wins. pendingSpeaker keeps its meaning.
  - The module gains speaker-ACK variables, and DeckSignature follows Stagewatch's ACK.
- G48: Patterns can pause and hold a playlist item or a stinger's clip, and publishes video.pausable/stoppable.
- G31: TLS first and a desk probe (after round 3).

TIER C/D
- G03/G33: the context reader keeps 512 characters of verb and words.
- G34 (KeyFor bind rules; the assistant does not propose these lines, with the reason).
- G35:
  - The Show Bus node profile sends HELLO, then the proof, then SUBSCRIBE OFF/CONTEXT.
  - The show's facts go untagged through EncodeFact, so PlayMap follows the blackout over the same link.
- G13 and G36 after round 3.

Gains: the operator gets no frozen times, no published passes (nor anything derived from one), a dark stage that stays dark, a failover that keeps keyed pages, one message box with honest receipts, and a deck that can set the link. Patterns gets four rounds (89-92). PlayMap gets a scoped exception request with four fixes, a papers fix now, and four packages after round 3. Stagewatch gets three small units: 413, the rig's stall, and rig message signals.

decisions.decision: One order by show risk: Patterns Round 89 holds only G04 and G09; Mapper's tier-A work and G25 go to the owner as one explicit exception request (PM-X); everything else waits for the Stagewatch release or round-3 integration pass it needs.
decisions.why: Four tier-A faults need no contract change; Patterns' units need no other repo; Mapper's round 3 §4 forbids edits to unnamed files, so the honest path is to ask.
decisions.alternatives: One interop round per repo (delays safety); reading §4 as allowing fix branches (the critique showed the fix-*-win precedent was CI stability, not new behaviour).

decisions.decision: G04: a volatile _stuck flag written only by the receive loop (set by {"type":"beat","live":false}, cleared by the next state frame, connect or Reconcile); the context moves to its own field written only by the beat task; the Sight getter composes both and sets Frame.Live=false and Stuck while stuck.
decisions.why: Today the beat task (StagewatchLinkService.cs:377) and the receive loop (:533) both read-modify-write one volatile record, so a context landing after a stuck beat restores the live frame and repeats the log line; one writer per field removes the race and makes one log line per transition true.
decisions.alternatives: Writing Live=false into _sight (the beat task undoes it); withholding the last-word refresh (pongs refresh it anyway); dropping the link.

decisions.decision: G04: a Stagewatch stuck before its first frame changes nothing on the stage — StagewatchSight.Stuck (init, non-positional) is set, Following stays false, the desk's timer and TIMER verbs stay, the words say why.
decisions.why: Creating a frame would make StageService.Following true (StageService.cs:61) and refuse the desk's TIMER verbs for a Stagewatch that never sent a time.
decisions.alternatives: An empty Unknown frame (the first draft; a silent behaviour change).

decisions.decision: G04 reaches every reader in one unit, including ShowAppCard.Of (red hue, 'its show is stuck') on the Nodes page; ShowBusTests.cs:374 is kept and the beat assertions added beside it.
decisions.why: Patterns' 'every reader' doctrine; the card colours by state alone (StagewatchFollow.cs:299-310); the live:false parse path still exists.
decisions.alternatives: Deleting the :374 assertion (weakens coverage).

decisions.decision: G09: kept://host[:port]/<id> with a 60-bit id from RandomNumberGenerator, stored with the URL in the per-machine book; the same normalised URL kept again reuses its entry by lookup.
decisions.why: An unsalted hash over a URL whose pass is a 4-digit ?pin= (rig default 4321) or a free-text ?view= code is brute-forceable from the published id; a random id is not a function of the URL.
decisions.alternatives: SHA-256 of the URL (the first draft); an HMAC under a per-machine secret (a second secret file for no gain).

decisions.decision: G09 and the twin: patterns.webpasses.json lives in SettingsStore.BaseDirectory; a new TwinWord KEPT carries the whole book main → standby on welcome and on change only when TwinConfig.SendSecrets is on; the standby merges into its own book; with SendSecrets off the standby draws kept pages black with words (OPEN L60, a §22 walk row).
decisions.why: A standby takes the show (TwinService.cs:11-20), including a same-machine standby with its own --home (TwinLauncher.cs:18); the twin already carries device secrets under this switch (L36).
decisions.alternatives: 'Never twinned' beside the exe (the first draft: breaks failover, bypasses BaseDirectory, two writers of one file).

decisions.decision: G09 readers added: WebFrameSource.cs:1402 failure log and _status name the held address; OscService._lastLine shows WindowAddresses.RedactText(line); WebVideoService resolves a held page before the tool and VideoEngine.cs:331 names Origin; the support bundle passes every text entry through RedactText and lists the kept file in NeverBundled.
decisions.why: Each carried the pass to a published reader (the Eye's OSC node, the log in the bundle).
decisions.alternatives: Rewriting backups/ and rotating logs at migration (backups are the undo path and are not bundled; the bundle is what leaves the machine).

decisions.decision: G09's remainder (STATE to unpaired wire peers) closes in Round 90.2 with spec-1-3's unit, and that unit changes RemoteTrustTests.Wire and the ShowBusAppTests helpers to pair first.
decisions.why: After 89 nothing secret rides STATE; the helpers assert 'STATE {' first on a token desk with TrustLoopback=false (RemoteTrustTests.cs:71-78).
decisions.alternatives: Closing it in 89 (couples a safety fix to the 1.3 contract).

decisions.decision: Mapper: PM-F1..F4 are an explicit exception request (PM-X) quoting round 3 §4 in full; EngineCore.Content.cs (four G47 sites, no hunk slot) lands before W3 begins if granted; declined, all four move to the integration pass and SHOWBUS-NODE says not to paste a window address.
decisions.why: §4: 'A folder not named for a wave keeps no owner in it, and nothing in that wave edits it' (PLAN.md:2124-2125); §5.7 is for missing seams; W1 is built and W3 has not begun.
decisions.alternatives: Fix branches as of right (misreads §4); a ≤10-line hunk in an owner's slot (no slot exists, and the change is larger).

decisions.decision: G47: refuse page, embed and private-address imports without echo; Redacted shows a private-address word as ‹private address›; at engine start a Web/Embed item with a private location is renamed '<host> ‹private address›' with its location cleared in one journalled edit; https .m3u8/.mpd filed as Stream with its https decode stated as unproven; the catalogue row words and FakeEngineLink.cs:697 go to the integration pass as notes.
decisions.why: A refusal is journalled through Redacted (EngineCore.Control.cs:172-175); items already holding a pass publish it in MEDIA LIST, STATE and the context, which Redacted does not reach.
decisions.alternatives: SecretFrom on MEDIA IMPORT (hides every path, misses SET … location).

decisions.decision: G12 air half on the exception: blackout and watermark appended to STATE's timer and drawn; the desk's StateSnapshot and the assistant's StateExplainer take them at the integration pass (wave-owned files).
decisions.why: A lit timer in a blackout is an air fault and a missing mark a licence fault; App and Assistant are not PM-F's to edit.
decisions.alternatives: windows-for-peers' single PM-W2 after round 3.

decisions.decision: G25: fit by bytes only. A context ≤65,536 bytes is posted byte for byte; over it: recent texts cut to 200 characters, then command words dropped from the end, then green and grey items; a grey context:trimmed item and link words; still over → not posted. Per-count 1.3 limits stay the integration pass's.
decisions.why: The only measured wall is Stagewatch's 64 KiB refusal (WebServer.cs:457, :1613); its reader truncates rather than refuses (ShowBus.cs:97-103) and keeps 200 characters of recent, so step one loses nothing it reads.
decisions.alternatives: Fitting to spec-1-3's counts (the first draft: governs what was not measured).

decisions.decision: Stagewatch 413: a declared body over 64 KiB on a non-deferred path is drained (≤1 MiB, 10 s) and answered 413 JSON, then closed; the upload and script paths keep their own caps; a declared body over 1 MiB is closed undrained; no chunked claim.
decisions.why: Closing with unread data resets the connection on Windows (WebServer.cs:1533-1536 comment), so the sender would never read the 413; HttpRequest has no Transfer-Encoding support.
decisions.alternatives: 413 then close unread (the first draft).

decisions.decision: G21 route: while following, a speaker message goes via Stagewatch only when the link is Live and holds a key not known to be read-only; otherwise it is shown on this desk's displays with words saying Stagewatch's do not show it. Flash maps to slow|off, urgency is info. The receipt's stage is read: applied+refs binds, accepted is journalled 'not yet applied' and binds on the frame, and 409/401/403/timeout falls back locally. CLEAR posts clearmessage only for a message Patterns posted.
decisions.why: Following needs no key (StagewatchLinkService.cs:269), and cue steps send STAGE MESSAGE (ShowActions.Stage.cs:20-22), so refusing would stop cue stacks. Message defaults to flash=true (StageService.cs:107). A slow show thread answers 200 'accepted' with no refs (ShowState.cs:1203, WebServer.cs:838-851). clearmessage would wipe the Stagewatch operator's own message.
decisions.alternatives: Refusing when the link cannot carry it (the first draft: breaks cue stacks).

decisions.decision: G21 readers: the page draws one speakerShown (latest wins between Stagewatch's current message and a desk-only one). pendingSpeaker keeps 'waiting for its ACK': a via-Stagewatch message clears when the frame's messageAck is seen or done. STATE appends speakerFrom/speakerAck/speakerAckBy; DeckSignature adds the frame's MessageId/MessageAck; the module adds stage_speaker_from, stage_speaker_ack and a feedback.
decisions.why: Stagewatch's message stays on screen after its ACK, so reusing pendingSpeaker would leave stage_pending lit falsely (feedbacks.js:227-232). DeckSignature is keyed on local ids (StageService.cs:201-205).
decisions.alternatives: pendingSpeaker carrying Stagewatch's message (the first draft).

decisions.decision: G21 sends on a SpeakerLane task per connection through the link's HttpClient, one request in flight, latest wins per channel, results posted to the UI thread.
decisions.why: The beat task runs ping, context and approvals one after another with a 4 s timeout each (StagewatchLinkService.cs:289, :328-355).
decisions.alternatives: Posting from the beat task's gate (the first draft: seconds of latency).

decisions.decision:
G34 KeyFor: node:<id> | addr:<host>:<port> | none | '' (unbound).
- It is bound when the key is typed on the Nodes page, or for an old key, to the configured host at load.
- An unbound key binds at the first 2xx to POST /api/peers/context, and only when the key is key-shaped.
- Any STAGEWATCH LINK line turns an unbound key to none.
- addr: re-binds to node: only over TLS with that node's pin held.
- The heard-id form is id:<id>.
- The ACCEPT prefix is a typing check against stale presses.
- LINK, FOLLOW and ACCEPT are high risk.
decisions.why: A line-set host must never receive a key that is not bound to it. A non-key-shaped value passes a Stagewatch that has no PIN (WebServer.cs:867-870); an unknown key-shaped key gets 401 (:1073-1082). A bare word parses as a host (StagewatchFollow.cs:192). FOLLOW OFF changes the speaker's air. A UDP hello alone must not move the key.
decisions.alternatives: Binding on any 2xx to /api/context (the first draft); FOLLOW at review; the binding rule following any hello.

decisions.decision: G34: Patterns' own assistant does not propose STAGEWATCH lines; the brief names them as the operator's.
decisions.why: Its proposals are typed show content (AssistantPage.cs:380-395); repointing a key-bearing link or the speaker's timer source is a trust decision like a certificate.
decisions.alternatives: A new assistant proposal kind for the link (rejected for this design; the gap's ask is declined with this reason in the papers).

decisions.decision: G48: PAUSE holds a playlist item's clock or a stinger's clip; STOP restarts and holds a playlist item; STOP on a stinger's clip stays refused toward STINGER STOP; video.pausable/stoppable appended; a schedule entry due during a hold fires at release inside its window, else journalled.
decisions.why: playout-links' Stagewatch link reads pausable instead of its role rule; the operator's hold is the newer explicit intent.
decisions.alternatives: Keep refusing.

decisions.decision: G03/G33: adopt cross-app-proposals' 15 appended rows. Patterns' context reader keeps 256 commands, drops a command whose verb is over 512 characters, and cuts words at 512. The brief lists 32.
decisions.why: One cap. PlayMap's busy golden has verbs up to 307 and words up to 403 characters, so all 199 commands and their words are kept.
decisions.alternatives: 200 characters of words (the first draft contradicted its own test).

decisions.decision: G35 ShowBusNode session: NONCE → HELLO Patterns <desk> → AUTH-PROOF over nonce+name → SUBSCRIBE OFF → SUBSCRIBE CONTEXT. Commands are tagged @d<n>. The show's facts go untagged through a new ProfileSession.EncodeFact, and only for PlayMap's FactLines keys (OPEN 1 is not sent). A STATE greeting is dropped and counted. A wrong token stops sends.
decisions.why: Tagged facts are read as verbs and refused (WIRE.md:105-106). Without HELLO, PlayMap's client table never lists the desk (WireSession.cs:153). Untagged facts from a paired peer reach PlayMap's air under FOLLOW-BLACKOUT.
decisions.alternatives: Tag everything (the first draft); no HELLO; HearsShow off (loses blackout following over the link).

decisions.decision: G31, G13, G36 after round 3 as first designed (G31 with peers-not-screens PM-1; G13 on the owner's decision 7; G36 minimal), plus a Mapper contract test against Patterns' Show Bus node session.
decisions.why: Spine and wave-owned files; owner calls.
decisions.alternatives: Fix branches (not bugs).

decisions.decision: Stagewatch gains SW-RM: rig message signals, receipts with refs.messageId, frames carrying messageId/messageAck/messageAckBy, and ack. message.e2e.cjs runs on peers-not-screens' --node-keys (SW-6) and is the contract Patterns' FakeStagewatch copies.
decisions.why: Today the rig's receipts carry no refs (Program.cs:191), ack is not simulated (:217), and its frames carry no message signal (:258-290).
decisions.alternatives: An e2e in wire.e2e.cjs against today's rig (cannot pass); a --node-key-file option (no such unit exists).

decisions.decision: Round numbers are the maintainer's; this design fixes the order and maps the siblings' guesses in §9.
decisions.why: The safety units must land first, and two sibling designs cannot both be Round 89.
decisions.alternatives: Keep the siblings' numbers.

revised.wire:
PATTERNS

Round 89.1 (G04). Nothing new is sent. Patterns reads Stagewatch's existing bytes {"type":"beat","live":false} (repeated every 2 s while stuck).
- STATE bus.stagewatch appends, across rounds: stuck (89), key (90), follow and pending (91), windows (92).
- While stuck, with a frame held: "text":"", "light":"red", "words":"following Stagewatch Hall A — it says its show is stuck; the time is not shown", "stuck":true.
- While stuck with no frame yet: "following":false, "light":"red", the words "… this desk's own stage timer runs until its first frame", "stuck":true.
- /api/stage follows appends "stuck".
- The twin relay is unchanged (frame.live rides in it already).
- Companion: variable stagewatch_stuck = yes|no, and a red feedback stagewatch_stuck.
- Log, one line per transition: "Stagewatch link: Hall A says its show is stuck — the stage shows no time." and "… Hall A's show runs again."

Round 89.2-89.3 (G09). No verb.
- STATE web: {"page":"10.0.0.5 (private address, kept)","url":"kept://10.0.0.5:9924/<id>"}. The id is 12 base32 characters from RandomNumberGenerator, stored in the book, and reused for the same URL.
- residency.holds[].key: "web:kept://…"
- Eye and CONTEXT id: "source:web:kept://…"
- WEB OPEN <private url> replies with the host only.
- OSC status line: "/patterns/web/open → WEB OPEN http://10.0.0.5:9924 (private address) → OK …"
- patterns.webpasses.json, in SettingsStore.BaseDirectory, at most 64 entries, NeverBundled: {"v":1,"passes":[{"id","url","keptUtc"}]}
- Twin, main → standby, only with TwinConfig.SendSecrets: the line `KEPT {"v":1,"passes":[…]}` on welcome and on every change; the standby merges it.
- Without the book, the page draws black and reads "(private address, kept on another machine)".
- Migration: one journal row.
- Support bundle: every text entry passes through WindowAddresses.RedactText, and the kept URLs join Secrets.Scrub.
- Private means:
  - a /w/ path of 26 window-alphabet characters;
  - a query or fragment word win|pin|token|key|view|code|secret|password|pass|apikey|api_key|access_token|auth|sig|signature;
  - user information in the address.

Round 90. As the siblings define it:
- the node link /ws?node=<id>&t=patterns with its auth verdict, and STATE bus.stagewatch.key;
- on a token desk, an unpaired non-loopback connection hears NONCE first and gets no STATE until OK paired, and Broadcast skips unpaired peers;
- the 15 context rows appended;
- Parse keeps 256 commands, drops a command whose verb is over 512 characters, and cuts words at 512.

Round 91.1 (G34).
- STAGEWATCH [STATUS] → OK {"on","state","name","address","follow","tls","keyFor","pending"}
- STAGEWATCH LINK AUTO|ON|OFF|<host[:port]>|id:<heard id>
- STAGEWATCH FOLLOW ON|OFF
- STAGEWATCH ACCEPT <at least 8 hex>
- STAGEWATCH KEY … → ERR "The Stagewatch key is typed on the Nodes page only — it never rides a line"
Risk: LINK, FOLLOW and ACCEPT are high. None is listed in the context. Refused from origin (Tcp,"approval desk").
Key presentation:
- KeyFor is node:<id> | addr:<host>:<port> | none | "".
- The key is presented only when KeyGoesTo is true.
- A line turns an unbound key to none.
- A key binds at the first 2xx of POST /api/peers/context with a key-shaped key.
STATE bus.stagewatch appends follow and pending. Module: actions stagewatch_link, stagewatch_follow, stagewatch_accept; variables stagewatch_follow, stagewatch_pending.

Round 91.2 (G21). Patterns → Stagewatch on the speaker lane: the link's HttpClient, scheme, host, port and pin.
Requests:
- POST /api/message/<text, one percent-encoded segment, ≤500>/info/<slow|off>/ack
- POST /api/clearmessage, only for a messageId Patterns posted
- POST /api/ack/<messageId>/seen/<desk ≤40>
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, X-Request-Id: pt<n>.
Replies:
- 200 receipt, stage "applied", with refs.messageId
- 200 receipt, stage "accepted", no refs
- 409 receipt
- 401/403 {"ok":false,"error"}
Patterns' answers:
- via Stagewatch: Requested, "OK requested: to Stagewatch Hall A's speaker: '…' — its receipt and the speaker's ACK come back here";
- otherwise: Done, "… on this desk's displays only; Stagewatch Hall A's displays do not show it (the link holds no node key | the key may read but not send messages | Stagewatch Hall A is quiet)".
Journal rows: on the speaker's screen (message 41) / accepted, not yet applied / refused (…) — shown on this desk's displays only / superseded / seen by … / "Stagewatch Hall A's own message stays — clear it there".
STATE and pages:
- STATE stage appends speakerFrom (stagewatch|desk|""), speakerAck (""|requested|accepted|sent|seen|done|refused) and speakerAckBy.
- pendingSpeaker is unchanged in meaning.
- /api/stage appends speakerShown {id ("sw:<id>" or a local id), text, flash, from}; follows appends messageId, messageAck, messageAckBy.
- The pages draw speakerShown and acknowledge its id.
Module: variables stage_speaker_from, stage_speaker_ack; feedback stage_speaker_ack_is.

Round 91.3 (G48). STATE video appends pausable and stoppable after seq.
- VIDEO PAUSE on a playlist item → OK "'opener.mp4' paused at 1:02 — the playlist holds with it; VIDEO PLAY runs both on"
- VIDEO STOP on a stinger's clip → ERR "… is a stinger's clip — STINGER STOP puts the show back"

Round 92.1 (G35). DeviceProfile.ShowBusNode on TCP:
← NONCE <hex>
→ HELLO Patterns <desk>  ← OK
→ @dp AUTH-PROOF <hex(HMAC-SHA256(normalised Secret, nonce + "Patterns <desk>"))>
← OK @dp paired | OK @dp open — … | ERR @dp wrong token (sending stops)
← STATE {…} (dropped and counted)
→ @do SUBSCRIBE OFF
→ @dc SUBSCRIBE CONTEXT  ← CONTEXT {…} on every change
→ @d<n> <verb line>  ← OK|ERR @d<n>
→ untagged facts, only PlayMap's FactLines keys (BLACKOUT 0|1, LIVE, LOOK, CUE …); OPEN 1 is never sent.
Kind words: playmap → PlayMap; peers row t:"playmap".

PLAYMAP (Mapper; PM-F1..F4 only on the owner's exception, PM-X)

fix-stagewatch-timer-air (G12):
- STATE links.stagewatch.timer appends, after why: "blackout":bool,"watermark":"StageWatch by Ben Rohleder".
- Later fields append in this order: next, urgency, flash, flashTimer, holding, holdingName, holdingFill, timeOfDay, show.
- The surface draws black under blackout and always draws the watermark.

fix-media-page-import (G47):
- MEDIA IMPORT <private url> → ERR "that address carries a pass … — PlayMap keeps no such address: draw Stagewatch's timer with SURFACE SOURCE <surface> timer:stagewatch, or send the page as NDI from a browser"
- MEDIA IMPORT <page> or an embed → ERR "a web page needs a browser source, which PlayMap has not built (docs/ROADMAP.md L10) — send it as NDI, OMT or Spout"
- https .m3u8/.mpd → OK added (stream; https decode unproven)
- Any shown line: a private-address word becomes ‹private address›.
- At engine start, a pass-bearing Web/Embed item is renamed "<host> ‹private address›" and its location cleared, with one journal row.
- MEDIA LIST for a web item: ready:false, state "unplayable", words.
- MEDIA FETCH → ERR "… is a web page PlayMap cannot draw — never fetched".

fix-stagewatch-context-size (G25):
- The body sent to POST /api/peers/context is at most 65,536 bytes. A context at or under that is sent byte for byte.
- Trimming order: recent texts to 200 characters, then command words, then green and grey items.
- When trimmed, the body carries {"id":"context:trimmed","kind":"health","label":"Context trimmed","light":"grey","state":"…"}, and links.stagewatch.detail adds " · context trimmed for Stagewatch (…)".
- When it cannot fit, nothing is posted: "this node's context is N KB after trimming — over Stagewatch's 64 KB; not posted".
- A 413 reads "Stagewatch refused the context as too large (413)".

After round 3:
- G31: as first designed (TLS first, 403-then-wss words, desk probe GET /api/proposals?target=<id>&state=approved every 60 s).
- G13: cross-app §2.9.
- G36: TIMECODE SOURCE ADD <name> PATTERNS and LINK PATTERNS SEND <line…> (high risk; AUTH, AUTH-PROOF, NONCE, HELLO and SUBSCRIBE refused; Redacted journal).

STAGEWATCH
- SW-25: a declared Content-Length over 65,536 on a path other than /api/holding/upload and /api/slides/script:
  - the body is drained (up to 1 MiB, 10 s), then 413 {"ok":false,"error":"a request body is at most 64 KB"}, then close;
  - over 1 MiB, the connection closes without draining;
  - no body is logged; no chunked support is claimed.
- SW-ST, rig only: a stdin line 'stall <ms>' → {"rig":"stalled","ms":…}, then {"rig":"running"}.
- SW-RM, rig only:
  - a message with ack makes a signal, and its receipt carries refs.messageId;
  - frames carry messageId, messageAck and messageAckBy;
  - ack <id> seen|done <by> moves the signal; a new message cancels the old one; clearmessage clears.
  - Node keys come from peers-not-screens' --node-keys N.
- Proposed for spec-1-3 §13: beat.stuck {"type":"beat","live":false}.

Auth summary:
- Patterns → Stagewatch HTTP uses the link's key in a Bearer header, only to a target KeyFor matches.
- Device links pair by HMAC proof over nonce + hello name.
- Kept passes travel only on the key-proved twin link under SendSecrets.
- STAGEWATCH verbs need a paired wire connection and are refused from the approval desk.

issues.issue: G09: the kept id leaks the low-entropy secrets the design's own private rule names. The id is an unsalted, deterministic, 60-bit truncation of SHA-256 over the full normalised URL, and it is published in STATE web.url, residency keys, Eye ids, CONTEXT (which is also posted to Stagewatch) and the show file. The rule treats ?pin=, ?view=, ?code= and ?pass= as private, but Stagewatch's PIN is a short digit string (the rig's default is 4321) and its viewing code is free text an operator types. kept:// already publishes host and port, and the paths are guessable (/timer, /stage, /countdown). issues.issue: G21: routing STAGE MESSAGE to Stagewatch while following turns a working local path into refusals and wrong facts. That includes cue steps ('Sent by a cue'), so cue stacks fail mid-show. The offered way out, STAGEWATCH FOLLOW OFF, also drops the timer. (b) The path is hard-coded /info/off, but Patterns' Message defaults to flash=true. (c) When Stagewatch is stuck or slow, it answers 200 {ok:true, stage:'accepted'} with no refs after 3 s. Receipt() returns only (Ok, MessageId, Error), so an accepted receipt is journalled 'on the speaker's screen'. (d) STAGE CLEAR posting clearmessage wipes the Stagewatch operator's own speaker message, not just the one Patterns sent.

Add tests for each case.

issues.issue: Stagewatch 413: the design sends '413 then close, the body unread'. Stagewatch's own code says why that fails: closing with unread data makes Windows reset the connection, and the client sees a network error instead of the answer. PlayMap's fit-or-413 words would then never arrive. Also: (1) as written ('a declared Content-Length over 65,536 → 413') it would refuse holding-image uploads (25 MB) and slide scripts, which have their own larger caps on the deferred paths; (2) 'a chunked body that runs past 64 KiB is answered the same' is wrong, because HttpRequest has no Transfer-Encoding support at all.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1533-1546 (SkipDeferredBodyAsync and its comment on resets); :1599-1606 (UploadPath and ScriptPath read deferred with their own caps); :1607-1609 (length > MaxBody returns null); no 'transfer-encoding' anywhere in Timer.Remote; design §3.3.
issues.fix: Drain the declared body (bounded, with a timeout) before writing 413, as SkipDeferredBodyAsync does, and exempt the deferred paths. Drop the chunked claim. The unit test should use a real HttpClient on a real socket and assert the client reads the 413, not a reset.

issues.issue: G35 (Round 92): ShowBusNodeSession tags every encoded line @d<n>. So the facts turn into ERR replies, counted as the device's refusals, and PlayMap's following of Patterns' blackout through the device stops.
